correctness.rationale: A forbidden geodesic triple consists of two vertices in the same part and one in another; the complex is the join of the discrete parts with each full part simplex glued along exactly its discrete vertex set. The join is connected and each point attachment map can be homotoped to a constant in the homotopy pushout, yielding a_i−1 extra circles per part. The join of the pointed discrete parts has the asserted product number of top spheres, including a cone for a singleton. For two parts the two wedge counts add to a_1a_2−1. For t≥3 the pair sequence uses H_1 of the join zero and relative homology supported only in degree one, giving the natural direct sum of augmentation lattices and preserving top homology. Ordered join chains show that a permutation of part factors multiplies by its sign on the top tensor. The recorded finite Betti and Lefschetz checks are corroboration only, not an independent replay or a substitute for this integral proof.
